newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's king mediating release of Hamas leaders.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king mediating release of Hamas leaders.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan is working for the release on humanitarian grounds of two jailed leaders of the Palestinian militant group Hamas, a cabinet minister said on Friday.

"His Majesty is undertaking contacts with Israeli and American officials to release Sheikh Yassin and Dr Abu Marzook on humanitarian reasons," Justice Minister Abdul Karim al-Dughmi told Jordan television.
Sheikh Yassin, the ailing 61 year-old spiritual leader of Hamas, was jailed by Israel in 1989 and is serving a life sentence for ordering attacks by Hamas guerrillas against Israeli targets.

Dughmi also said a U.S. judicial team would be arriving in Amman next week to hold "detailed talks" on the case of Hamas leader Mousa Abu Marzook, who has been in a New York prison since his expulsion from Jordan in June 1995.

On Thursday, Israeli security sources confirmed a newspaper report that Israeli, Jordanian and U.S. officials were secretly examining a deal to send Abu Marzook to Jordan in return for a promise from him to shun violence.
Dughmi declined however to say if Abu Marzook would be allowed back.
Israel has alleged that Abu Marzook, as political leader of Hamas, was responsible for attacks, including by suicide bombers on public buses, that killed scores of Israelis.
Last month, Abu Marzook dropped his court challenge to the Israeli request for his extradition, in effect agreeing to be sent to Israel.
Hamas warned from Gaza it would attack Israelis if Abu Marzook was extradited. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat asked the United States not to send him to Israel.
